MeasureTheory.cLpNorm.statement: Let $\alpha$ be a measurable space and $E$ a normed additive commutative group. For $p \in [0,\infty]$ (an extended nonnegative real) and a function $f : \alpha \to E$, $\mathrm{cLpNorm}(p, f)$ is the real number $\mathrm{lpNorm}(f, p, \mu)$, the $L^p$ norm of $f$ with respect to the measure $\mu = \mathrm{uniformOn}(\alpha)$, the uniform measure on all of $\alpha$ (counting measure on $\alpha$ normalised by the number of elements of $\alpha$, a probability measure when $\alpha$ is finite and nonempty). Its docstring describes it as the $L^p$ norm with the compact normalisation.
